Specifying a model

One formula carries the equations of all the parameters of the distribution, separated by a bar, and the terms of each equation come from modelterms7.

statmod_spec()
Build a Model Specification
statmod_equations()
Split a Multi-Parameter Formula Into One Equation Per Parameter
statmod_design()
The Design of a Specification

Fitting

One formula and one distribution. The coefficients of the terms with a differentiable penalty are fitted in one system, together with a score-driven term, and the terms with a kinked penalty and the regime terms are alternated with that system. The section also holds the inner method, the criteria for the hyperparameters and the simulator.

statmod()
Fit a Model

reml() ml()

cv()

rstatmod()

print(<StatmodSim>)
Printing a Simulation

The information matrix and the solver

The matrix that the inner fit inverts, that enters a Laplace determinant or that gives the standard errors is passed as an object: the observed Hessian and the expected (Fisher) information, both defined in distributions7, or a choice settled against the family. The factorization that solves each step is passed as an object too, with its numerical tolerances.

Where a fit begins

A starting value given as a strategy and not as a vector of numbers, and evaluated once before the fit alternates. The default builds the start from intercept-only fits; the other strategies are procedures, from a random perturbation to a global search of the likelihood to the estimates of a model already fitted.

Intervals of a prediction

The argument interval of predict() takes an object that selects the uncertainty that the interval describes: the estimates alone, the estimates and the effects of a new group, or a new observation of the response. A prediction interval holds a second object that sets how the estimation uncertainty enters the predictive distribution.

Testing a coefficient

One coefficient against one value, by Wald’s statistic, the likelihood ratio, Rao’s score or Terrell’s gradient. summary(test =) reports the same four for every row against zero, and confint(test =) inverts them; statmod_test() also takes a null value other than zero. The test that a break-point exists is a separate function, which reads the supremum of a score process over the positions of the break-point.

statmod_test()
Test One Coefficient Against One Value
statmod_breakpoint_test()
Test That a Break-Point Exists

Test statistics

The four statistics with which a coefficient is tested, as objects passed to the argument test of statmod_test(), summary() and confint(): Wald’s, the likelihood ratio, Rao’s score and Terrell’s gradient. The overview states the formula of each, what it needs and what it costs, and test_restricted() tells whether a statistic refits the model under the restriction.

gradient_test()
Terrell's Gradient Test of a Coefficient
test_restricted()
Whether a Test Refits the Model Under the Restriction

Profile likelihood

The penalized log-likelihood, or the outer criterion, maximized over every quantity but one or several that are held on a grid, returned as a StatmodProfile object with its intervals (confint()) and its graphs. The grid of values is given by profile_range() or by the caller, and profile_grid() selects the exact method, one refit for each point; profile_continuation() and profile_taylor() approximate it for smooth coefficients.

Variance conventions

Graphs of a fit

plot() and autoplot() draw one aspect of a fit as a ggplot2 object. The graph is selected by an object passed as type, and its data are computed by plot_data() and drawn by plot_layers(), the two generics through which a new graph is added. Without a type, plot() draws the diagnostic graphs of diagnostics().
